issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex lacks /i flag while sibling HAS_KEYWORD has it, complecting case-sensitivity rules across notations
issues.detail: PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS likely contains 'from'/'to' or percentages; HAS_KEYWORD uses /i but HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. The two regexes encode two different time/identity assumptions about what counts as a match. Either case matters everywhere or nowhere -- the asymmetry is incidental complexity smuggled in via copy-paste.

issues.description: Fast-path regexes and the authoritative parser are now two sources of truth for the same fact
issues.detail: Each rule now has a regex predicate ('does this value contain a named weight?') and a valueParser/selector-parser that answers the same question authoritatively. These are complected: a future keyword added to fontWeightNonNumericKeywords must also be reflected in HAS_NAMED. The value (keyword set) and the identity (the predicate) have drifted apart. Add a test that derives one from the other, or compute the regex lazily from the canonical set in one place.

issues.description: import-notation url() detection ignores comments and strings, conflating syntactic appearance with semantic presence
issues.detail: /url\(/i.test(params) matches inside /* url( */ comments or quoted strings like "url(". For 'string' mode this causes a false skip (rule won't flag a real violation); for 'url' mode a false skip too. The regex treats textual occurrence as identity of a url() token. Either anchor more carefully or accept that the parser must run -- but the current shortcut is essential-vs-incidental confusion.

issues.description: selectorRegex = /./ sentinel is place-oriented thinking; a missing filter expresses 'no filter' more simply
issues.detail: The else branch assigns /./ so walkRules always matches. This complects two concerns: 'no fast-path available' and 'fast-path is match-anything'. Cleaner: keep selectorRegex undefined and branch on its presence at the walk site, or have two walk calls. The /./ is easy, not simple.

issues.description: media-feature prefix regex /[<>]/ may match inside string tokens or comments in at-rule params
issues.detail: Same shape of issue as url(): the predicate treats character occurrence as syntactic identity. For media query params this is likely safe in practice, but the pattern is now repeated across five files without a shared note about its assumptions. Worth a one-line comment naming the assumption (params are pre-stripped of comments) so the next maintainer doesn't reapply it where it breaks.

issues.description: The right question: why is the parser slow on negative cases at all?
issues.detail: Every fast-path here exists because parseSelector/valueParser is expensive even when there is nothing to do. The simple fix is making the parsers cheap on trivial inputs; the easy fix is sprinkling regex guards in every *-notation rule. The PR ships the easy fix, which is fine, but it scatters the parser-cost concern across many rules instead of fixing it in one place. Worth tracking as a follow-up.

review.summary: This PR is a pragmatic performance win, but it is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: each rule now carries a hand-tuned regex that duplicates a fact the canonical parser already knows, and the two will drift. The keyframe HAS_PERCENTAGE/HAS_KEYWORD case-sensitivity asymmetry is a real bug risk. The import-notation and media-feature guards substitute textual appearance for token identity, which is the kind of complecting that bites later. The deeper question -- why parseSelector and valueParser are slow on trivial input -- is being answered by scattering guards across five files rather than fixing the cost at the source.
